question: Worsening of a known opportunistic infection 4–8 weeks after starting ART in a severely immunocompromised patient indicates that the antiretroviral regimen is failing.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually false. The scenario describes Immune Reconstitution Inflammatory Syndrome (IRIS) — the recovering immune system (responding to effective ART) mounts a strong inflammatory response against the pre-existing pathogen, causing paradoxical worsening. IRIS is NOT treatment failure; it signals immune recovery. It is most common with TB and Cryptococcus, occurring 4–8 weeks after ART initiation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Paradoxical worsening of a known OI shortly after starting ART is most likely Immune Reconstitution Inflammatory Syndrome (IRIS), not treatment failure. The recovering immune system mounts a vigorous inflammatory response against the existing pathogen. IRIS is commonest with TB and Cryptococcus and typically occurs 4–8 weeks after ART initiation.
